**Pantone “Sky Blue” – common reference points**

| # | Pantone Code | Typical description / use case |
|---|--------------|--------------------------------|
| **A** | **PANTONE 290 C** | Very light, almost pastel‑blue often used as a “soft sky” background. |
| **B** | **PANTONE 292 C** | Slightly deeper than 290 C but still very airy—good for subtle gradients. |
| **C** | **PANTONE 293 C** | A bit more saturated; frequently chosen when you want a true “mid‑day sky.” |
| **D** | **PANTONE 294 C** | Even richer, closer to a clear summer day’s horizon. |

> *If your design brief calls simply for “sky blue,” most designers default to PANTONE 290 C because it captures the classic pale hue people imagine.*

---

### Quick conversion guide (CMYK)

| Pantone | Approximate CMYK* |
|---------|------------------|
| 290 C   | C = 0%, M = 12%, Y = 30%, K = 0% |
| 292 C   | C = 0%, M = 18%, Y = 35%, K = 0% |
| 293 C   | C = 0%, M = 25%, Y = 40%, K = 0% |
| 294 C   | C = 0%, M = 32%, Y = 45%, K = 0% |

\*These CMYK figures are rounded approximations from Pantone’s official data sheet; actual output may vary depending on printer/ink set.

---

#### How to choose:

| Situation | Recommended Shade |
|-----------|--------------------|
| **Soft backgrounds & UI elements** | 290 C |
| **Print brochures needing a gentle pop** | 292 C |
| **Brand identity where “sky” feels vibrant yet calm** | 293 C |
| **High‑contrast prints (e.g., billboards)** | 294 C |

Feel free to test each one under your lighting conditions—sometimes what looks “sky blue” on screen differs subtly from print. If you’re working digitally, you could also try hex `#87CEEB` (a web‑safe approximation) which aligns closely with Pantone 290 C.
